title: SGA: Self-boosting Attributed Graph Alignment via Neighborhood Consistency-based Edge Enhancement

problem.claim: Graph alignment identifies corresponding nodes across different graphs and supports applications such as social network analysis and bioinformatics.

gap.claim: Existing attributed-graph alignment methods often use objectives designed for node classification or link prediction, preserving within-graph node proximity but failing to capture cross-graph correspondence knowledge.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph alignment is important for identifying corresponding nodes across graphs and has applications in social network analysis and bioinformatics.
Existing methods commonly use GNNs to learn node embeddings and match nodes by similarity, with objectives oriented toward node classification or link prediction.
These methods preserve node proximity within individual graphs but do not capture cross-graph correspondence knowledge, resulting in suboptimal alignment performance.
